answer: One defense is a refundable stake that vests slowly, like a glacier rather than a flood: each agent locks tokens that unlock only after sustained useful work, so creating thousands of fake identities means tying up capital for every one. Honest agents ride the normal tide of transactions and earn their stake back, while a sybil operator faces multiplied cost and delayed payoff. A shared registry can also flag a nebula of brand-new accounts acting in lockstep, raising the stake required for that cluster before it can transact.
